questions.stem: What is a key advantage of using CNF in automated satisfiability solving?

options.text: It simplifies the implementation of SAT solvers.
It reduces the number of variables in a formula.
It always minimizes the formula size.
It is the only form that can express logical equivalences.

questions.explanation: CNF provides a uniform structure that is easier for SAT solvers to process. It does not inherently reduce variables or minimize size, but it simplifies solver implementation.

distractorRationale.b: CNF does not necessarily reduce the number of variables; it provides a uniform structure.
distractorRationale.c: Conversion to CNF can increase the formula size.
distractorRationale.d: Logical equivalences can be expressed in forms other than CNF.

questions.stem: Explain why converting a formula to CNF can lead to a size blow-up. Provide an example to illustrate your explanation.
markingGuide: Explanation of the blow-up phenomenon due to distribution.
Example illustrating the exponential increase in size.
Discussion of nested structures contributing to blow-up.
questions.explanation: Converting to CNF involves distributing disjunctions over conjunctions, which can exponentially increase the number of clauses. For example, converting \((A \lor B) \lor (C \land D)\) to CNF results in \((A \lor B \lor C) \land (A \lor B \lor D)\), doubling the number of clauses.

questions.stem: Which logical equivalence is used to eliminate implications in CNF conversion?
questions.explanation: To eliminate implications, we use the equivalence \(A \to B \equiv \neg A \lor B\). This step is crucial in converting to CNF.

questions.stem: Discuss the importance of CNF in the context of SAT solvers. Why is CNF preferred over other forms?
markingGuide: Discussion of algorithmic efficiency in SAT solvers.
Comparison with other forms and their complexities.
questions.explanation: CNF is preferred in SAT solvers because its uniform structure allows for efficient algorithmic processing. This form simplifies the implementation of solvers and is well-suited for the DPLL algorithm. Other forms may introduce complexities that are harder to handle algorithmically.

questions.stem: Which of the following transformations is necessary when converting a formula to CNF?

options.text: Applying De Morgan's laws to conjunctions.

questions.explanation: The key transformation in CNF conversion is distributing disjunctions over conjunctions, which aligns the formula into a conjunction of disjunctions.

distractorRationale.b: Converting conjunctions to disjunctions is not used in CNF conversion.
distractorRationale.c: De Morgan's laws are applied to negations, not specifically to conjunctions.
distractorRationale.d: Negations are not eliminated; they are managed using De Morgan's laws.
